purpose: a focal that can be read off a hand must come from the hand's 3D SHAPE. These controls destroy that shape in three different ways while leaving everything else identical. If the solver still recovers the focal under a control, the signal is not geometric and the positive result is an artefact.

controls.what: randomly permute the 21 reference-3D joints before the solve, keeping the 2D order fixed
controls.destroys: the joint correspondence, hence all shape information
controls.expected_if_signal_is_real: the solver should fail or return a flat, uninformative profile

controls.what: replace the reference 3D by the reference 3D of the SAME hand in a DIFFERENT, temporally distant frame of the same view
controls.destroys: the match between 3D pose and 2D observation, while keeping a real hand's scale and bone lengths
controls.expected_if_signal_is_real: large focal error; this is the sharpest control because hand SIZE is preserved

controls.what: orthogonally project the reference 3D onto its own best-fit plane before the solve
controls.destroys: the depth extent that makes perspective, hence focal, observable at all
controls.expected_if_signal_is_real: the profile should become flat or the optimum should run to the grid boundary, because a planar target cannot separate focal from depth

reporting_rule: every control is reported with the same metrics as the main condition, in the same table, whatever the outcome
